The titles are large because the majority of the titles posted are song or album names and not long sentences. In absolute terms they are no larger than, say, video titles on YouTube (both about 28px tall at default zoom). Other text is not larger than the rest of the site, just more consistently sized; e.g. metadata is same size as body text but differentiated by colour, instead of being smaller by 1-2px which creates a very messy, ragged look on the default styles.

Moving the votes and score to the right was an experiment, to emphasise the content and not the score. Yours is the first (negative?) feedback about it. I will probably bring back the default voting arrows as they are clearer, but I’m inclined to leave them on the right.

Moving the expando button to the right was also an experiment. I may try to position it over the thumbnail instead.

The full-width container is oddly controversial, but it’s ultimately more usable to have it full-width and allow users to resize their browser window, than have it fixed at an arbitrary width (where users will have to use browser stylesheets or third-party extensions to change said arbitrary width). If it’s too wide, narrow your window; it takes 1 click or a keyboard shortcut with most OSes.

If you think any of the custom CSS has a negative impact on usability I will definitely fix them, but otherwise aesthetic changes are fair game. The default stylesheets are themselves an evolving jumble of code without a clear design plan, with often inconsistent styles, so I see no reason to be attached to them.
